summary: Remote-controlled agent exposes shell, filesystem, git, and network proxy over WebSocket
details: When `yeaft-agent` (bin) or `node index.js` is executed, the process connects to a configured WebSocket server and dispatches remote messages to privileged local handlers. A `terminal_input` message writes its `data` field directly into a PTY spawned as the OS shell (`process.env.SHELL || 'bash'` on POSIX; `pwsh.exe`/`powershell.exe`/`cmd.exe` on Windows), giving whoever controls the server full interactive shell access to the host. The same message router also dispatches `read_file`, `write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `copy_files`, `git_add`, `git_commit`, `git_push`, and `proxy_request`/`proxy_ws_open`/`proxy_ws_message`/`proxy_ws_close` to workbench and proxy handlers, allowing the remote party to read/write arbitrary files in the agent's workdir, mutate and push git state, and tunnel arbitrary HTTP/WS traffic through the installer's network. The behavior fires at tool startup, not on `npm install` or on `require()`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
